title: Integrations and AI
context: Choose one external integration and one bounded AI capability only when they improve the core workflow, then make failure safe and observable.

stories.title: Choose integrations by user value and risk
stories.outcome: The release contains only justified external dependencies.
stories.context: Compare proposed email, webhook, payment, automation, and AI capabilities against the primary workflow, baseline alternative, cost, failure, security, and lock-in.
acceptanceCriteria: At least three proposed capabilities are evaluated
One integration and at most one AI capability are selected or explicitly rejected
ADR defines provider, baseline, budget, failure behavior, disable path, and data boundary

expectations.privacy: List exactly what leaves the application.
expectations.accessibility: Core workflow remains usable when provider is down.

stories.title: Implement a reliable provider integration
stories.outcome: The selected email, webhook, payment, or automation capability completes safely and reports failure clearly.
stories.context: Use server-only credentials, provider-specific verification, validation, idempotency where needed, and synthetic test fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: Credentials and webhook secrets remain server-only
Inbound events are authenticated according to official provider docs and validated
Duplicate/retried events cannot duplicate the business action
Provider outage leaves core data consistent and gives an actionable state
stories.dataContract: Validated provider event mapped to internal command/result.

expectations.privacy: Send minimum fields and redact logs.
expectations.analytics: Provider status and latency without payload.

stories.title: Ship a bounded AI capability
stories.outcome: AI improves one specific task without becoming an unreviewed decision-maker or hard dependency.
stories.context: Compare to a deterministic baseline. Use structured output, narrow context, explicit token/cost limit, adversarial evaluation, and fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: Feature purpose and non-AI baseline are documented
Output is runtime validated and unsafe/unavailable output falls back safely
Evaluation set covers normal, edge, injection, malformed, timeout, and cost-limit cases
Feature can be disabled without breaking the core product
stories.dataContract: Versioned input/output schema with no unnecessary personal data.

expectations.security: Treat user/retrieved text and model output as untrusted.
expectations.privacy: Record provider retention policy; minimize prompts/logs.
expectations.accessibility: Label AI output and provide correction path.
expectations.analytics: Latency, cost, fallback, user acceptance without prompt content.

stories.title: Prevent duplicate provider side effects
stories.outcome: Repeated delivery produces one intended business result.
stories.context: Elena replays the same synthetic event twice and observes duplicate rows or notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: A regression test reproduces the duplicate before the fix
Stable provider event ID or idempotency key prevents duplicate processing
Concurrent and failed-then-retried behavior are documented
stories.dataContract: Persist processed event identity where needed.

expectations.security: Verification still runs before duplicate handling.
expectations.analytics: Duplicate delivery may be operationally counted.

stories.seededBug: Process the business action before recording the provider event ID, allowing the same event to run twice.
